title: Backlog.md: Terminal Kanban Board for Managing Tasks with AI Agents — Alex Gavrilescu, Funstage

primary.label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 83%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is Backlog.md's MCP server exposing tools and resources to AI agents for task management, fitting tool calling and protocol design. Backlog.md is a developer tool for managing coding tasks with AI agents, placing it in developer platforms and coding assistants. The tool is presented as a production-ready, deployed system used for real software engineering workflows. The content assumes familiarity with Git, MCP, and AI agent workflows but is accessible to practitioners. The presentation includes live terminal demonstrations of task creation, implementation planning, and feature execution. All claims are directly stated in the transcript with supporting excerpts.

summary: Alex Gavrilescu introduces Backlog.md, a terminal Kanban board tool that stores tasks as Markdown files in Git repositories, designed for both AI agents and humans. The motivation stems from problems where AI agents work for extended periods only to run out of context window or pursue wrong directions. The solution involves dividing large features into smaller atomic markdown tasks with clear descriptions, acceptance criteria, and implementation plans. Backlog.md uses an MCP server to expose resources including workflow overview, task creation guide, task execution guide, and task completion guide. It also exposes MCP tools for searching, viewing, creating, and updating tasks. The workflow involves three review checkpoints: after task creation, after implementation plan creation, and after code implementation. Tasks stored as markdown enable context engineering, allowing precise control over how much an agent implements per task. The demonstration shows Claude creating a move-mode feature task, generating an implementation plan, and implementing the code. The tool supports parallel task work via git worktrees when no dependencies exist. Backlog.md is open-source under MIT license, cross-platform, requires no external APIs or databases, and synchronizes task status across branches. Notably, 99% of the codebase was written by AI agents, with Gavrilescu only writing instructions and the first three tasks.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Motivation
sections.summary: Gavrilescu introduces the problem of AI agents running out of context window or going in wrong directions, and presents Backlog.md as a solution for managing tasks for AI agents and humans.

sections.title: Terminal Kanban Board Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates the terminal Kanban board showing tasks across columns with task details including descriptions, acceptance criteria, and implementation notes visible in-terminal.

sections.title: Defining Requirements for Move Mode Feature
sections.summary: Specifies clear requirements for the move-mode feature: M key to toggle, arrow keys to reorder and change status, enter/M to commit, escape to cancel, with footer instructions.

sections.title: Claude Creating the Task
sections.summary: Claude reads Backlog.md documentation, understands how to create tasks, and creates a markdown task file with frontmatter metadata, description, and acceptance criteria. This is the first review checkpoint.

sections.title: Implementation Plan Creation
sections.summary: Claude creates an implementation plan by researching documentation and codebase. This is the second and most important review checkpoint where engineers verify the agent's direction.

sections.title: MCP Server Architecture
sections.summary: Explains the MCP server exposing resources (workflow overview, task creation guide, task execution guide, task completion guide) and tools (search, view, create, update tasks) for AI agents.

sections.title: Task Execution Workflow
sections.summary: Describes the execution workflow where agents implement acceptance criteria and move tasks to Done. Reviews the overall human-AI workflow from task creation to implementation.

sections.title: Implemented Feature Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates the implemented move-mode feature working correctly, showing task highlighting, reordering, status changes, commit, and cancel functionality.

sections.title: Why Backlog.md Works Well
sections.summary: Explains context engineering benefits: atomic tasks prevent context exhaustion, clear scope via acceptance criteria, three review checkpoints, and parallel work via git worktrees.

sections.title: Backlog.md Overview and Conclusion
sections.summary: Summarizes Backlog.md as open-source MIT CLI tool with terminal and web interfaces, MCP and CLI support, cross-platform, no databases needed, Git-based sync, and 99% AI-written code.

demonstrations: Terminal Kanban board showing tasks in To Do, In Progress, and Done columns with task details
Claude creating a move-mode feature task with description and acceptance criteria
Claude generating an implementation plan identifying files to modify
Claude implementing the move-mode feature allowing task reordering and status changes
Testing the implemented move feature with keyboard navigation (M, arrow keys, enter, escape)
limitations: Implementation plan generation takes time as agent searches documentation and codebase
Parallel task work requires no dependencies between tasks
